Preliminary U.S. trade screening

Selling into the U.S.? Know where you stand on duty, deadlines and risk.

Effective 2027-01-05 · CBP rule for a foreign importer of record (FR 2026-22735) · Read the rule

A free, event-driven screen for importers and overseas sellers: possible duty-recovery questions, CBP notices (CF-28 / CF-29), AD/CVD exposure and general U.S. import risk. It tells you what may be wrong, what money and dates may matter, what fact is missing and when a licensed professional should look. The PlaudeAPI code runs in your browser: it asks for no documents, uploads nothing, and stores nothing on any server.

Start with what happened

  • Duty / recovery / liquidation Could there be a U.S. duty recovery opportunity? Is there a possible deadline? Entries that paid IEEPA-era duties, overpaid duty, or are approaching liquidation.
  • CF-28 / CF-29 CBP notice risk check You received a Request for Information or a Notice of Action from CBP.
  • AD/CVD AD/CVD exposure pre-screen Your product or origin may fall under an antidumping / countervailing duty order.
  • General U.S. import risk U.S. customs risk check You are starting to sell into the U.S. and want to know which measures may touch your product.

Paid service

Trade diagnostic

One service at one flat fee, in one of two scopes; each engagement covers one scope. Refund scope: the report on your IEEPA duties described in the next paragraph. IOR status scope: a written analysis of one entity's U.S. IOR / foreign IOR status under 19 CFR 110.2, and of the entry arrangements available under 19 CFR 141.21(b) or, for a U.S. IOR, 19 CFR 141.22(a); $495 for one entity, within the same 5 business days after we receive the complete inputs listed under Turnaround below.

A flat-fee written report by Bandi & Associates PLLC, computed on your own ACE entry report, entry by entry: which IEEPA duties are still unrecovered; which route, if any, remains for each entry (a declaration in CAPE, CBP's process for IEEPA refund declarations, which only the importer of record or the broker that filed the entry can file and Bandi & Associates PLLC does not; the certified class; or your own action at the Court of International Trade); and what has to happen on which date, where a published CBP rule fixes the date. $495 for one importer of record with up to 50 entries; larger files are quoted before we start. Written analysis within 5 business days after we receive the complete inputs listed under Turnaround below.

  • What you get

    Refund scope

    Entry-by-entry table from your ACE entry report: entry number, entry date, liquidation date or status, the CAPE window for each entry, IEEPA duties deposited, refund status and the route for each of your entries Dated events: the date each liquidated entry's CAPE window closes and the IEEPA duties on that entry; entries not yet liquidated show the window as open, with no computed date The route question for your company: which entries CAPE can still take, which depend on the class the Court of International Trade (CIT) certified in October 2026, and what filing your own CIT action would change Who receives the refund: CBP certifies refunds for payment to the importer of record, or to a party it designates on CBP Form 4811 (19 C.F.R. 24.36). If your courier, broker or U.S. buyer was the importer of record and no owner's declaration was filed, CBP pays that importer of record, or the party that importer of record designates on Form 4811, unless a surety paid the duties (19 C.F.R. 24.36(a), (b)); whether you can recover from that importer of record is a separate question, and the report says what to ask that importer of record for in writing. If you were the importer of record yourself, including as a non-resident, the refund right is yours; CAPE then needs ACE access or your filing broker, and the ACH payment needs a U.S. bank account or a Form 4811 designee Status of the IEEPA refund litigation and CBP's process as of the report date, each statement with its source and the date we read it What Bandi & Associates PLLC can do for you next, for example a letter to the courier or other importer of record, with a fee quote (separately engaged)

IOR status scope: a written analysis of one entity's U.S. IOR / foreign IOR status under 19 CFR 110.2, on where it is organized and located, its ownership and control structure and its U.S. real-property situation; and of the entry arrangements available to it under 19 CFR 141.21(b) or, for a U.S. IOR, 19 CFR 141.22(a), given its current customs broker and that broker's CTPAT status.

An AI chatbot is not bound by those Rules and owes you neither duty under them One federal court in New York (Heppner, S.D.N.Y.) held in February 2026, in a criminal case, that a person's own conversations with a public AI chatbot about his legal exposure were not protected by the attorney-client privilege.   • Turnaround A written analysis within 5 business days after we receive the complete inputs: your ACE entry report with the date on which each entry's duties were paid; your broker's CAPE acceptance reports and refund records, or "none"; whether you were the importer of record on the entries; and your statements whether an owner's declaration was filed on any entry and whether you have filed any protest or court action. Missing inputs stop the clock; we name what is missing within 1 business day of receiving your file. The same list is in the engagement terms you accept before you pay.

How it works

Book a 15-minute call, or start with names only: your name, your company, the other parties involved (for example your courier, customs broker or U.S. buyer) and a case number if you have one. Do not send facts yet. Bandi & Associates PLLC runs a conflict check first; payment and the booking link follow only after the conflict check is cleared and you have accepted the engagement terms.

If you are located in China, tell Bandi & Associates PLLC before you send any document that contains personal information about individuals (for example consignee names, addresses or phone numbers); the diagnostic does not need that information.
